feat: v9.0.0 — three new agent templates (Discovery, Stakeholder Comms, Launch)
This release adds three new agent templates to the library, bringing the total to four.

New templates:
- PM Discovery Agent: synthesises customer interviews from Notion or Google Drive,
  identifies cross-interview themes, scores assumption confidence, generates follow-up questions
- PM Stakeholder Comms Agent: detects audience type (executive/investor/stakeholder/board),
  pulls activity from Linear/Jira/Drive, drafts in audience-appropriate format
- PM Launch Agent: end-to-end launch coordination with channel-specific content,
  calendar, success metrics, and launch checklist

Each template follows the established pattern: README, AGENT.md, orchestrate.sh,
2 subagents, connectors with example configs, examples, smoke test.

Total file count: 37 new files across 3 templates.

fix(skillpack): correct path-traversal check for pack member paths (#192)

'p.startsWith(resolve(dir))' is a classic path-traversal-check flaw:
resolving 'dir=/tmp/foo' against 'path=../foo-evil/skills/x/SKILL.md'
yields '/tmp/foo-evil/skills/x/SKILL.md', which starts with '/tmp/foo'
and passes the check even though it points *outside* the pack. RFC-0001
says the runtime MUST reject such packs.

Use 'path.relative(base, p)' and reject when the relative path is
empty, starts with '..', or is absolute — the standard containment
check on POSIX and Windows.

fix(reckoning): accept confidence 0, 1, and 100 in the calibration ledger (#193)

The parser silently dropped valid confidences from the Brier score:

- 'conf > 1 && conf < 100' rejected the endpoints (0% 'sure miss',
  100% 'sure hit') even though they are legitimate — and useful —
  points on the calibration curve. It also rejected 1%, the
  natural 'near-sure miss'.
- 'parseFloat(meta.confidence)' returned NaN on missing values, but
  'if (!conf)' also treated 0 as missing, so a stated 0% was
  discarded and later 'searched for (\d{1,2})%' in the body — which
  further couldn't match '(100%)'.

Fix: use Number.isFinite gating (so missing != 0), widen the body
regex to \d{1,3}, and clamp to [0, 100].

fix(lib/anthropic): tolerate CRLF in parseSkill frontmatter (#194)

parseSkill is called by 'run' and 'chain'. With LF-only regex, a
SKILL.md authored on Windows fell through to 'text.trim()' — the entire
file (including the raw '---' frontmatter block) became the system
prompt, wasting tokens and diluting the skill's instructions. Match the
CRLF-tolerant regex already used in scripts/skillcheck.mjs and
bin/cli.mjs.

fix(lib/scheduler): escape XML in plist and shell-quote crontab values (#195)

Two related quoting bugs in the scheduler feeding Nightwatch and
subscribe:

macOS/launchd plist — process.cwd() and each arg in argvArray were
inserted raw between '<string>…</string>' tags. A cwd containing '&',
'<', '"' etc. (real on paths like '/Users/foo/A&B') produced malformed
XML and 'launchctl load' rejected the plist. Fix: xml-escape the five
metachars.

Linux crontab line — 'cd ${process.cwd()}' was unquoted, so a cwd
with spaces broke the line. Each arg was JSON.stringify'd, but that
uses *double* quotes where '$var', backticks and '\\' are still
expanded by bash. Fix: POSIX single-quote quoting with the '\''
trick.

skillcheck as a GitHub Action, and as a published command

The validator that keeps 1,099 skills here honest now runs against anybody's.
Skill authoring is new enough that the mistakes are the same handful, and all
of them are cheap to catch: a description with no "Use when …" clause, a
frontmatter name that does not match its folder, template text nobody deleted.

- bin/skillcheck.mjs is the one implementation. It gained --dir (with
  auto-detection across skills/, .claude/skills/, src/skills/ and the root),
  --json, and GitHub workflow annotations with real line numbers — so a finding
  lands on the line in the PR diff instead of in a log nobody opens.
- scripts/skillcheck.mjs is now a thin wrapper pointing at it, so this repo is
  checked by exactly the same rules everyone else's is. Shipping a linter that
  exempts itself is not honest.
- `npx pm-claude-skills skillcheck` exposes it; scripts/ is not published, so
  the old location could never have been reached from outside.
- action.yml at the root, pinned to ^76.0.0. An action floating on `latest`
  breaks every user the day a major lands.
- .github/workflows/skillcheck-action.yml dogfoods it against these 1,099.

Two things fixed while testing it as a stranger would:

- `--dir` on a path that does not exist crashed with a raw ENOENT out of
  readdir instead of saying which directories were searched.
- a repo with zero SKILL.md folders exited 0. A CI step that was asked to check
  skills and found none is a misconfiguration, not a pass — silently succeeding
  there is how a broken pipeline goes unnoticed for months.

Verified from a clean directory against the published package: outputs
populate, 15 annotations emit, exit 1 on failure and 0 on pass.

vitals: stop the data branch failing a Vercel Preview every day

The daily "vitals: <date>" Preview deployment has failed every run since at
least 2026-08-21. Production was never affected, which is why the commit
statuses on main all read success.

Cause: repo-vitals.yml force-pushes vitals-data daily, and that branch is data

tools: contradiction sweep over the 6,039-rule anti-pattern corpus

The handbook compiles every skill's Anti-Patterns into one body of professional
judgment. Nothing had ever checked it was internally consistent, and at 1153
skills written over months, two of them advising opposite things is a question
of when rather than whether.

Two stages, because contradiction is not decidable by string matching and
pretending otherwise ships a tool that cries wolf:

  recall (free, offline) — reduce ~18 million possible rule pairs to ~96 by
  finding rules where one forbids roughly what another prescribes
  judge (--judge, costs tokens) — an LLM rules agree / contradict / unrelated
  on each candidate, and only that stage produces findings

Getting stage 1 honest took three attempts, and each failure is now encoded in
the code as a comment rather than left as a trap. Treating an anti-pattern's
polarity as a property of the rule was wrong — every line in that section is
already a prohibition, so "restating the error instead of explaining it" reads
as two opposing rules when it is one. And "do not ship without tests" embeds a
requirement: the clause after until/without/unless is prescribed, not
forbidden. Before that fix the top of the report was entirely skills agreeing
with each other about named owners.

The output says plainly that stage 1 is a shortlist and not a finding, because
a tool that overstates its confidence is worse than no tool.

fix(zapier): read platformVersion from the installed package (#281)

The app hard-coded platformVersion as 15.0.0. Zapier rejects an app
whose platformVersion differs from the installed zapier-platform-core,
so any update to that package would have broken the push. It is now
read from the package. Checked against 15.0.0 and 15.19.0.
